description:
Issue summary: Engineering attempted to assume the ops-to-customer cross-account role to run a debug job on a private LLM node and received 'AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole' despite role trust and policy appearing correct.

Impact: On-call engineers cannot run targeted diagnostics or rotate KMS keys for the private deployment in eu-west. This blocks a critical support path for private customers and delays a security patch rollout.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-scoped VPC) in eu-west-1. Role is in account: 987654321001 (dedicated/private). Caller originates from ops account: 123456789012. Attempt was made from platform-provisioner pod in prod cluster.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From ops account, run aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::987654321001:role/RedwoodCrossAccountSupportRole --role-session-name debug-session
2) Observe AccessDenied error.
3) Confirm role exists and attached policies allow kms:Decrypt and s3:GetObject.
4) Check AWS Organizations SCPs and OU-level deny rules via admin account.

Observed behavior / Logs: see logs field.

Expected behavior: ops account should be able to assume the support role when allowed by the customer's trust policy and not blocked by organization-level denies.

Initial hypothesis: An AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) at the customer OU is denying sts:AssumeRole or kms:Decrypt for the role/principal, causing the request to be rejected even though the role trust policy is permissive. Another possibility: a condition on the role requiring specific source-account or external ID that the ops token did not present.
logs: 2026-03-09T14:22:03Z ERROR sts AssumeRole failed: AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource arn:aws:iam::987654321001:role/RedwoodCrossAccountSupportRole
CallerIdentity from ops account before assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/platform-provisioner
aws-cli debug trace shows AssumeRole call returned HTTP 403 with AccessDenied body
investigation_notes: Checked role trust policy in target account: Principal includes arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root and sts:ExternalId condition NOT present.
Confirmed inline policies attached to role permit kms:Decrypt and s3:GetObject for relevant resources.
Queried AWS Organizations from admin account and found an SCP 'deny-external-assume' applied at OU level; SCP denies 'sts:AssumeRole' unless the source is an allowlisted account tag.
Customer OU SCP appears to be a new policy pushed by SecOps last week (audit snapshot 2026-03-05).
Attempted a test assume-role from a different ops account (tagged allowlisted) — succeeded, indicating an allowlist gating in SCP.
No VPC endpoint or network-level blocks detected — API calls reach STS and return AccessDenied.
GCP check: Not applicable for this artifact; private deploy uses AWS in eu-west for this customer.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Filed after first failed diagnostic run. Need help unblocking the support role so SRE can rotate KMS and run model mismatch diagnostic on customer node.
Marco Ruiz (2026-03-10): I can reproduce. Gathering SCP list from org admin. Assigning to myself to coordinate with SecOps.

Nisha Verma - SecOps (2026-03-11): Noted: we rolled out 'deny-external-assume' to several sensitive OUs to prevent lateral access. We can add ops account to allowlist if justified. Please provide ticket with justification and timebound window.
Marco Ruiz (2026-03-11): Added justification in thread and requested temporary allowlist for ops account 123456789012 for 4 hours to run diagnostics and key rotation. Pending SecOps approval.
workaround: SecOps can temporarily add ops account 123456789012 to the SCP allowlist or create an exception via an allow policy applied at the OU for a timebound window. Alternatively, run diagnostics by launching a support session from an already allowlisted account (requires cross-team coordination).
next_steps: SecOps to review and approve a 4-hour allowlist exception for ops account 123456789012 or provide alternative path.
If approved, SRE to re-run assume-role and validate kms:Decrypt operations against the private node and rotate keys if needed.
Update runbook: document SCP exceptions process and include checklist for private-deploy debug access to avoid repeated fire drills.
Post-incident: propose an automation to request timebound SCP exceptions via internal portal with audit trail.
